tEn: On Kimi K3: Its Capabilities And Related Discontents
tZh: 论 Kimi K3：其能力及相关不满
sEn: Kimi K3 is genuinely impressive but sits on the expected capability curve, roughly three to eight months behind leading proprietary models, and the discourse around it is often shaped by motivated reasoning.
sZh: Kimi K3 确实令人印象深刻，但大致处于能力曲线的预期位置，落后领先闭源模型约三到八个月，而围绕它的讨论往往受动机性推理驱动。
absEn: This article assesses Kimi K3, a 2.8-trillion-parameter open-weight model from Moonshot, against the recurring narrative of a second DeepSeek moment. It argues that although Kimi K3 is genuinely impressive and posts strong benchmark results, it sits roughly where one would expect on the capability curve rather than representing an unexpected leap, with estimates placing it about three to eight months behind leading proprietary models such as Mythos Preview, Claude Fable 5, and GPT 5.6 Sol. The piece contends that discourse around Chinese open models is often driven by motivated reasoning, including desires to commoditize inference, discredit AI regulation, or declare America's lead erased on the basis of a single benchmark, and it warns that such claims have repeatedly influenced policy. It further notes that open models are relatively strongest on narrow, short-horizon coding tasks that are approaching saturation, while longer-horizon tasks relevant to AI R&D automation and cyber attacks show a smaller but still real gap, and that bio-risk testing for open models is conspicuously absent. The conclusion is that open models will eventually match frontier general capability, likely within a few months, and that this convergence, not any single release, is what should drive preparation.
absZh: 本文评估了 Moonshot 推出的 2.8 万亿参数开放权重模型 Kimi K3，并将其置于反复出现的“第二个 DeepSeek 时刻”叙事中加以审视。文章认为，尽管 Kimi K3 确实令人印象深刻，并取得了强劲的基准测试成绩，但它大致处于人们预期中的能力曲线位置，而非一次出人意料的跃升；据估计，它落后于 Mythos Preview、Claude Fable 5 和 GPT 5.6 Sol 等领先闭源模型约三到八个月。文章指出，围绕中国开放模型的讨论往往由动机性推理驱动，包括希望将推理商品化、贬低 AI 监管，或仅凭单一基准就宣称美国的领先地位已被抹平；文章警告，此类主张已多次影响政策。文章进一步指出，开放模型在狭窄、短周期的编程任务上相对最强，而这类任务正接近饱和；在与 AI 研发自动化和网络攻击相关的更长周期任务上，差距较小但仍然真实存在；此外，针对开放模型的生物风险测试明显缺位。结论是，开放模型最终将追平前沿通用能力，很可能就在几个月内；真正应当驱动准备工作的，是这一趋同趋势，而非任何单次发布。

full.sec: DeepSeek Moments: Here We Go Again

paras.en: All discourse about Chinese models lives in the shadow of the DeepSeek moment.
paras.zh: 所有关于中国模型的讨论都笼罩在 DeepSeek 时刻的阴影之下。

paras.en: There are a lot of people who really, really want another DeepSeek moment to happen.
paras.zh: 有很多人真的、真的非常希望再出现一个 DeepSeek 时刻。

paras.en: These people really, really want to tell the story that Chinese open models are catching up to American closed models, that AI and inference will become commoditized.
paras.zh: 这些人真的、真的非常想讲述这样一个故事：中国的开源模型正在追赶美国的闭源模型，AI 与推理将走向商品化。

paras.en: Their motivations vary. They often want to affirm open models, or the importance of the 'tech stack.' Others simply want to see OpenAI and Anthropic go down, or know that such claims sell. Often the ultimate objective is to argue against all AI regulations, or anything that might 'slow us down' or cause us to 'lose to China.'
paras.zh: 他们的动机各不相同。他们往往想肯定开源模型，或肯定“技术栈”的重要性。另一些人则只是想看到 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 倒下，或者知道这类说法有市场。通常，最终目的是反对一切 AI 监管，或反对任何可能“拖慢我们”或让我们“输给中国”的东西。

paras.en: It is actively suicidal to respond to 'the Chinese have better models now' with 'then we had better sell them the compute so they can run them and also build even better ones.' Yet every time, yes, people will argue that. Sigh.
paras.zh: 用“那我们最好把算力卖给他们，让他们能跑这些模型，还能造出更好的模型”来回应“中国人现在有更好的模型了”，这简直是自寻死路。然而每一次，是的，人们都会这样论证。唉。

paras.en: Often they simply want to tell American AI to stop taking precautions, to stop being annoying and take down the classifiers, as in 'genie is out of the bottle, so release the bigger genie with unlimited wishes, it's the only way.' People really would take major catastrophic risks rather than deal with classifiers, and are Big Mad about this.
paras.zh: 他们往往只是想告诉美国 AI 别再采取预防措施，别再那么烦人，把分类器撤掉，就像在说“精灵已经从瓶子里出来了，那就放出那个愿望无限的更大精灵吧，这是唯一的办法。”人们真的宁愿承担重大灾难性风险，也不愿应付分类器，而且对此非常愤怒。

paras.en: Google was down 4.4% on the day, SpaceX was down 3.1% and Nvidia down over 2%, and tech stocks were down again on Friday, so plausibly we're doing this again.
paras.zh: 当天 Google 下跌 4.4%，SpaceX 下跌 3.1%，Nvidia 下跌超过 2%，科技股周五再次下跌，所以很可能我们又要重演这一幕了。

paras.en: And yep, we are at risk of doing this again:
paras.zh: 而且没错，我们正面临重演这一幕的风险：

paras.en: Axios (being wrong): China just erased America's AI lead
paras.zh: Axios（说错了）：中国刚刚抹平了美国在 AI 上的领先优势

paras.en: Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh: No it didn't. (although Kimi K3 is undoubtedly impressive)
paras.zh: Seán Ó hÉigeartaigh：并没有。（尽管 Kimi K3 无疑令人印象深刻）

paras.en: 2. There is some impressive benchmark cited.
paras.zh: 2. 文中引用了一些令人印象深刻的基准测试。

paras.en: 3. Therefore, America’s lead is gone, QED, that’s it, no, really, that’s it.
paras.zh: 3. 因此，美国的领先地位已经不复存在，证明完毕，就是这样，不，真的，就是这样。

paras.en: In the Axios case the benchmark in question is Arena. Based on that alone, they state as fact that America’s lead is gone.
paras.zh: 在 Axios 的案例中，所讨论的基准测试是 Arena。仅凭这一点，他们就断言美国的领先地位已经不复存在。

paras.en: I would ignore, but this style of logic has convinced a lot of Washington D.C. multiple times, and that has had substantial policy impact.
paras.zh: 我本会忽略，但这种逻辑风格已经多次说服了华盛顿特区的许多人，并产生了重大的政策影响。

paras.en: I shudder to think what such folks might do now that they also know about Mythos. The confusion over Fable jailbreaks could easily extend to a broader dumb panic.
paras.zh: 想到这些人现在也知道了 Mythos，我不禁不寒而栗。对 Fable 越狱的困惑很容易演变成更广泛的愚蠢恐慌。

paras.en: The original DeepSeek moment happened because of a confluence of events.
paras.zh: 最初的 DeepSeek 时刻是多种事件共同作用的结果。

paras.en: Since then, the idea that China had caught up, or was catching up, kept coming up and drove much discussion around Washington, as echoes of this one moment.
paras.zh: 自那以后，“中国已经追上”或“正在追上”的说法不断出现，并作为这一时刻的回响，在华盛顿引发了大量讨论。

paras.en: This is then renewed every time a new strongest or exciting Chinese model comes out. Every day that China does not release a model, they look one day farther behind. When they do release, they 'catch up' and look less behind.
paras.zh: 此后，每当中国推出一款新的最强或令人兴奋的模型，这种说法就会再度兴起。中国每有一天不发布模型，他们看起来就落后一天。而当他们发布时，他们就“追上了”，看起来没那么落后了。

paras.en: The top 10 such potential moments since r1 and before K3 were likely these:
paras.zh: 自 r1 之后、K3 之前，最有可能的 10 个此类时刻大概是这些：

paras.en: 4. GPT-5 (in reverse), which spooked a lot of people in highly stupid ways.
paras.zh: 4. GPT-5（反向来看），它以极其愚蠢的方式吓到了很多人。

paras.en: Mostly it's been Kimi and DeepSeek. Manus got a hype train going and spooked people, and GLM-5.2 was by far their strongest offering, putting GLMs on the map.
paras.zh: 主要就是 Kimi 和 DeepSeek。Manus 掀起了一波炒作热潮并吓到了人们，而 GLM-5.2 是它们迄今为止最强的产品，让 GLM 系列一举成名。

paras.en: Many of these were good models, but none fundamentally changed the game.
paras.zh: 其中许多都是不错的模型，但没有一个从根本上改变了格局。

paras.en: Roughly, since the DeepSeek moment, when DeepSeek was roughly eight months behind but had matched some key aspects faster via fast following, we have bounced around. For a while it looked like China was quite a lot behind.
paras.zh: 大致来说，自 DeepSeek 时刻以来——当时 DeepSeek 大约落后八个月，但通过快速跟随在若干关键方面更快地追平——我们一直在来回波动。有一段时间，看起来中国落后相当多。

paras.en: GLM-5.2 and Kimi K3 have been impressive. The current best estimate of the time gap is at its lowest point. Events in AI have accelerated all around, so it is not clear that the gap is fewer product cycles than before, and I half expect to be doing this again next week for Qwen. Kimi K3 is 2.8T and seems to still be solidly behind Mythos Preview, which was announced on April 7, so that provides a starting point lower bound of a three month gap.
paras.zh: GLM-5.2 和 Kimi K3 令人印象深刻。当前对时间差距的最佳估计处于最低点。AI 领域的事件在各方面都在加速，因此尚不清楚这一差距是否比之前少了几个产品周期，我甚至有点预期下周又要为 Qwen 再做一次这样的评估。Kimi K3 是 2.8T，似乎仍稳稳落后于 4 月 7 日发布的 Mythos Preview，这提供了一个三个月差距的起点下界。

paras.en: Ethan Mollick: Kimi is, as I have been saying, a very good model. But it is not a DeepSeek r1 moment, in that it is roughly where I would expect on the curve rather than an unexpected leap. It will be treated as a DeepSeek moment for a variety of reasons especially as more people hear about it.
paras.zh: Ethan Mollick：正如我一直所说，Kimi 是一个非常好的模型。但它不是一个 DeepSeek r1 时刻，因为它大致处于我预期曲线上的位置，而非意外的跃升。由于种种原因，尤其是随着越来越多的人听说它，它会被当作一个 DeepSeek 时刻来对待。

paras.en: Ryan Greenblatt, despite being pleasantly surprised by Kimi K3, estimates that the pretrain quality is about halfway between Opus 4 and Opus 4.5 based on forward pass math, but with some other advantages, so ~8 months behind, as one might expect.
paras.zh: Ryan Greenblatt 尽管对 Kimi K3 感到惊喜，但根据前向传播的数学估算，其预训练质量大约介于 Opus 4 和 Opus 4.5 之间，不过还有一些其他优势，因此如人们所料，大约落后 8 个月。

paras.en: The post-training is closer, at least in part because of distillation. Moonshot is clearly innovating, but it is also clearly distilling, both directly and also fast following via looking at outputs and copying techniques.
paras.zh: 后训练阶段的差距更小，至少部分原因是蒸馏。Moonshot 显然在创新，但也显然在蒸馏——既直接蒸馏，也通过观察输出、复制技术来快速跟进。

paras.en: UK AISI issued a report on everything prior to Kimi K3, showing the time gap for narrow cyber tasks narrowing somewhat over time. Their full report is here.
paras.zh: 英国 AISI 发布了一份关于 Kimi K3 之前所有情况的报告，显示狭窄网络任务上的时间差距随时间有所缩小。他们的完整报告在此。

paras.en: My understanding is that narrow and relatively easy coding tasks are where open weights models are at their relative strongest, and the benchmark here is approaching saturation.
paras.zh: 据我理解，狭窄且相对简单的编码任务是开放权重模型相对最强的领域，而这里的基准正接近饱和。

paras.en: Indeed, when you look at the full post, you get a different answer for longer tasks.
paras.zh: 确实，当你查看完整帖子时，对于更长的任务会得到不同的答案。

paras.en: UK AI Security Institute: On TLO, GLM-5.2 reaches as far as Opus 4.5, a model released less than 7 months before it, while DeepSeek's V4-Pro falls below Sonnet 4.5 (a sub-cyber-frontier model released 7 months before it). These results are broadly consistent across our other cyber ranges. Notably, GLM-5.2 reached step 7 with marginally fewer tokens than any other model on average, tracking Opus 4.6's trajectory to step 11 before stalling.
paras.zh: 英国人工智能安全研究所：在 TLO 上，GLM-5.2 达到 Opus 4.5 的水平，而后者比它早发布不到 7 个月；DeepSeek 的 V4-Pro 则低于 Sonnet 4.5（一个比它早发布 7 个月的次网络前沿模型）。这些结果在我们的其他网络靶场中大体一致。值得注意的是，GLM-5.2 以平均略少于任何其他模型的 token 数到达第 7 步，沿 Opus 4.6 的轨迹推进到第 11 步后才停滞。

paras.en: Longer tasks are more relevant in terms of both of the most important things to worry about: automation of AI R&D and cyber attacks.
paras.zh: 就两个最需要担忧的最重要方面而言——AI 研发的自动化与网络攻击——更长的任务更为相关。

paras.en: One might also worry about bio risks, even if that is not as in fashion, and it is a little concerning we don't see standard testing on that at all for the open models. That needs to be addressed. We do have the score on OpenAI's GeneBench-Pro via Andrew Ho. This measures judgment under long-horizon ambiguity in computational biology. Kimi K3 exceeded expectations. Mythos have not been tested. Fable refused most requests in the benchmark.
paras.zh: 人们或许还会担忧生物风险，即便这已不那么时髦；而我们对开放模型完全没有看到针对该风险的标准测试，这有点令人不安。这一点需要得到解决。我们确实通过 Andrew Ho 拿到了 OpenAI GeneBench-Pro 的分数。该基准衡量的是计算生物学中长期不确定性下的判断力。Kimi K3 超出了预期。Mythos 尚未接受测试。Fable 在基准测试中拒绝了大多数请求。

paras.en: Beating Opus and GPT-5.5 is impressive stuff. No previous open model came close. We are on the verge of doing some f*ing around and thus finding out. This is a place where plausibly not much happens until suddenly quite a lot happens.
paras.zh: 击败 Opus 和 GPT-5.5 是令人印象深刻的事。此前没有任何开放模型能接近这一水平。我们正处在即将“瞎搞一通”从而“一探究竟”的边缘。在这个领域，很可能在很长一段时间内什么都不会发生，直到突然之间发生很多事。

paras.en: The conclusion of 'open models will catch up to Mythos in general capability including the thing that currently makes it unique' is indisputable. That is coming, the question is when, and that will establish the effective gap. Given Kimi K3 we should expect this to happen a few months from now.
paras.zh: “开放模型将在通用能力上追平 Mythos，包括目前使其独一无二的那项能力”这一结论是无可争议的。这一天终将到来，问题只是何时到来，而那时将确立实际差距。鉴于 Kimi K3 的表现，我们应当预期这会在几个月后发生。

paras.en: If we take both ends of UK AISI's estimates, the pre-Kimi gap was 4-7 months, down from 6-10 months last year, in an area of relative strength. That's roughly a similar amount of progress gap in absolute terms, and everything is accelerating.
paras.zh: 如果我们取英国 AISI 估计的两端，那么在相对优势领域，Kimi 之前的差距为 4-7 个月，低于去年的 6-10 个月。按绝对值计算，这大致是相近幅度的进展差距，而一切都在加速。

full.sec: The Kimi K3 Announcement, Pitch and Basic Facts
full.secZh: Kimi K3 发布、宣传与基本事实

paras.en: 1. 2.8 trillion parameters, 16 of 896 areas active at once, which implies ~50B active. This is not easy to run locally, and won't be that cheap.
paras.zh: 1. 2.8 万亿参数，896 个区域中同时有 16 个处于激活状态，这意味着约 500 亿激活参数。这不容易在本地运行，也不会那么便宜。

paras.en: 2. $3.00/$15.00, modestly cheaper than Opus and Sol.
paras.zh: 2. 每百万 token 输入 3.00 美元、输出 15.00 美元，比 Opus 和 Sol 略便宜。

paras.en: 3. Subscription plans are $19/$39/$99/$199 per month. The larger buys have some modest advantages and quota scales linearly with price.
paras.zh: 3. 订阅方案为每月 19/39/99/199 美元。价格更高的方案有一些适度优势，配额随价格线性扩展。

paras.en: 6. Training cutoff is reportedly early 2026.
paras.zh: 6. 据报道，训练数据截止时间为 2026 年初。

paras.en: 8. All benchmarks run under maximum effort settings.
paras.zh: 8. 所有基准测试均在最大努力设置下运行。

paras.en: Kimi: Today, we are introducing Kimi K3 — our most capable model. Kimi K3 is a 2.8T-parameter model built on our Kimi Delta Attention and Attention Residuals, with native vision capabilities and a 1-million-token context window. It is the world's first open 3T-class model, designed for frontier intelligence across long-horizon coding, knowledge work, and reasoning.
paras.zh: Kimi：今天，我们推出 Kimi K3——我们能力最强的模型。Kimi K3 是一个 2.8T 参数模型，基于我们的 Kimi Delta Attention 与 Attention Residuals 构建，具备原生视觉能力和 100 万 token 的上下文窗口。它是全球首个开放的 3T 级模型，面向长程编程、知识工作与推理等前沿智能场景而设计。

paras.en: While its overall performance still trails the most powerful proprietary models, Claude Fable 5 and GPT 5.6 Sol, Kimi K3 demonstrated frontier-level performance across our evaluation suite, consistently outperforming other tested models.
paras.zh: 尽管其整体性能仍落后于最强大的专有模型 Claude Fable 5 和 GPT 5.6 Sol，但 Kimi K3 在我们的评测套件中展现出前沿级表现，并持续优于其他受测模型。

paras.en: Kimi.ai: Kimi K3 is now live on http://Kimi.com, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the Kimi API. Open Weights by July 27, 2026.
paras.zh: Kimi.ai：Kimi K3 现已在 http://Kimi.com、Kimi Work、Kimi Code 和 Kimi API 上线。开放权重将于 2026 年 7 月 27 日发布。

paras.en: K3 is built on Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes), two architectural updates designed to improve how information flows across sequence length and model depth.
paras.zh: K3 基于 Kimi Delta Attention（KDA）与 Attention Residuals（AttnRes）构建，这两项架构更新旨在改善信息在序列长度和模型深度上的流动方式。

paras.en: We have also scaled up Mixture of Experts (MoE) sparsity, effectively activating 16 out of 896 experts when paired with a Stable LatentMoE framework.
paras.zh: 我们还扩大了混合专家（MoE）的稀疏度，在配合 Stable LatentMoE 框架时，有效激活 896 个专家中的 16 个。

paras.en: Together with refined training and data recipes, these structural changes yield an approximate 2.5× improvement in overall scaling efficiency compared to K2, allowing the model to convert compute into intelligence more effectively.
paras.zh: 结合改进后的训练与数据配方，这些结构性变化使整体 Scaling（规模扩张）效率相较 K2 提升约 2.5 倍，使模型能够更有效地将算力转化为智能。

paras.en: As stated above, they claim strong official benchmarks, although short of Sol or Fable.
paras.zh: 如上所述，他们声称在官方基准测试中表现强劲，但仍不及 Sol 或 Fable。

paras.en: The ad, which Tyler Cowen called very positive and very good, falls flat to me, and contains zero useful information.
paras.zh: 这则广告被 Tyler Cowen 称为非常正面、非常出色，但在我看来却平淡无奇，且不含任何有用信息。

paras.en: We used to see rather explicit benchmaxxing. Labs would train on the test, or on the very narrow thing the test would cover, because we had a limited set of known targets. You had to know which labs did this, to what extent, when looking at numbers.
paras.zh: 我们过去常看到相当露骨的基准刷分（benchmaxxing）。实验室会在测试集上训练，或者针对测试所覆盖的极窄范围进行训练，因为我们已知的目标集合有限。在看数字时，你必须知道哪些实验室这样做、做到什么程度。

paras.en: Our benchmarking technology has improved, and now they collectively measure real things, and there are a variety of backups in case you aim too narrowly.
paras.zh: 我们的基准测试技术已经进步，如今它们共同测量真实的东西，而且有多种后备手段，以防你瞄准得过于狭窄。

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): on the subject of benchmaxxing — it seems benchmarking technology has gotten better recently, like most other technology. People are more skeptical and build these things more carefully. There's also an explosion of downstream coding customers building internal held-out evals.
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：关于基准刷分这个话题——基准测试技术近来似乎变好了，就像大多数其他技术一样。人们更加怀疑，也更谨慎地构建这些东西。此外，下游编程客户构建内部留出评估（held-out evals）的情况也呈爆炸式增长。

paras.en: Looking at the gestalt of different benchmarks is also valuable. Everything should be part of a map that fits into a common pattern that reflects the underlying territory.
paras.zh: 审视不同基准的整体形态（gestalt）也很有价值。一切都应成为一张地图的一部分，这张地图契合一种反映底层真实领域的共同模式。

paras.en: You can still absolutely benchmaxx without being as explicit as you used to be.
paras.zh: 你仍然完全可以进行基准刷分，只是不必像过去那样露骨。

paras.en: Benchmarks measure some types of abilities rather than others, and measure shallow rather than deep tasks, and exclude many valuable properties or potential liabilities. And some labs focus more on those aspects, or have more success on them, than others.
paras.zh: 基准测试衡量的是某些类型的能力而非另一些，衡量的是浅层任务而非深层任务，并且排除了许多有价值的特性或潜在隐患。而一些实验室比另一些更侧重这些方面，或在其中取得更大成功。

paras.en: You can also set effort to maximum for all the tests, which Moonshot did.
paras.zh: 你也可以把所有测试的 effort 都设为最大，Moonshot 就是这么做的。

paras.en: Think of the benchmarks as a lower bound. Kimi's benchmarks prove it is for real, and it could only underperform (or outperform) them by so much. I still expected, and continue to believe, that they modestly overstate Kimi K3's relative capabilities.
paras.zh: 把基准测试视为一个下界。Kimi 的基准成绩证明它是真有实力的，它最多只可能在这些成绩上下浮动这么多。我此前预期、并且现在仍然认为，这些成绩适度高估了 Kimi K3 的相对能力。

paras.en: On the closest thing we have to the One True Benchmark, Kimi K3 does well, confirming claims that overall this model has the third highest benchmarks:
paras.zh: 在我们最接近“唯一真基准”的评测上，Kimi K3 表现良好，印证了该模型整体基准排名第三的说法：

paras.en: Kimi K3 is (in a preliminary unofficial result) exactly on the Chinese trend line for the Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI), between Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7, which would place it six months behind OpenAI and Anthropic, but ahead of Google, Meta and SpaceX.
paras.zh: Kimi K3（在一项初步的非官方结果中）恰好位于 Epoch Capabilities Index（ECI）的中国趋势线上，介于 Opus 4.6 与 Opus 4.7 之间，这意味着它落后 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 约六个月，但领先于 Google、Meta 和 SpaceX。

paras.en: Kimi K3 highly impresses on Harvey LAB-AA all-pass rate, in first by a wide margin; I'd like to see a sanity check on this:
paras.zh: Kimi K3 在 Harvey LAB-AA 全通过率上表现极为亮眼，以较大优势位居第一；我希望对此做一次合理性检查：

paras.en: For criterion pass rate this is 94.6% vs. 93.6%, less of a gap but a win is a win.
paras.zh: 就标准通过率而言，这是 94.6% 对 93.6%，差距较小，但赢了就是赢了。

paras.en: Arena Frontend Code has Kimi K3 at #1 ahead of Fable 5 and Sol.
paras.zh: Arena Frontend Code 将 Kimi K3 排在第一位，领先于 Fable 5 和 Sol。

paras.en: Kimi K3 comes in third on VoxelBench for visual reasoning, behind Sol and Fable.
paras.zh: 在视觉推理基准 VoxelBench 上，Kimi K3 位列第三，排在 Sol 和 Fable 之后。

paras.en: Conspicuously missing are cybersecurity benchmarks like CyberGym. Cyber capabilities are not so divorced from coding capabilities, so we can guess.
paras.zh: 明显缺失的是像 CyberGym 这样的网络安全基准。网络能力与编程能力并非截然分离，因此我们可以做出推测。

paras.en: The closest I've found is Malte Ubl running it through DeepSec, a private cyber benchmark. It was a tier below Sol and similar to GPT-5.5. If that is accurate, then there will be some uplift to cyber attacks and the internet will in some ways be a more hostile place, but in other ways it will improve, and the tail risks are limited.
paras.zh: 我找到的最接近的参考是 Malte Ubl 用私有网络基准 DeepSec 对其进行的测试。它的水平比 Sol 低一档，与 GPT-5.5 相近。如果这一结果准确，那么网络攻击能力将有所提升，互联网在某些方面会变得更加敌对，但在另一些方面也会有所改善，且尾部风险有限。

paras.en: Parv Mahajan reports preliminary CyBench results, in that the benchmark was already saturated as of Opus 4.7 and Kimi K3 also saturates it, which lower bounds performance but doesn't say much else.
paras.zh: Parv Mahajan 报告了初步的 CyBench 结果：该基准在 Opus 4.7 时就已经饱和，而 Kimi K3 同样使其饱和，这给出了性能的下界，但除此之外说明不了太多。

paras.en: The official tech blog talks a lot about benchmarks, and some about features, and talks basically not at all about risks or mitigations.
paras.zh: 官方技术博客大量谈论基准测试，部分谈及功能特性，而几乎完全没有提及风险或缓解措施。

paras.en: No, they did not submit Kimi K3 for the 30-day review with the White House.
paras.zh: 不，他们并没有将 Kimi K3 提交给白宫进行为期 30 天的审查。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball: I guess the program really is voluntary.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball：我猜这个项目确实是自愿性质的。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball: I wonder if the California attorney general or the European Union AI office will seek to make Moonshot comply with their respective frontier AI regulations.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball：我想知道加州总检察长或欧盟人工智能办公室是否会寻求让 Moonshot 遵守各自的前沿 AI 监管规定。

paras.en: Moonshot has to deal with the CCP, which comes with its own issues. They presumably will not in practice comply with California or the EU, and I presume both California and the EU will not do anything about this for now. But yes, this is one point of potential pain, including risk for anyone using Kimi K3 commercially.
paras.zh: Moonshot 必须应对中国共产党（CCP），这本身就带来了一系列问题。他们大概不会在实践中遵守加州或欧盟的规定，而我认为加州和欧盟目前都不会对此采取任何行动。但确实，这是一个潜在的痛点，包括对任何将 Kimi K3 用于商业用途的人而言都存在风险。

paras.en: Sam has some good advice for how the UK, or others watching, would be wise to view and react to this. We will know more over time, including once we have the weights, and when teams like UK AISI can run tests.
paras.zh: Sam 给出了一些很好的建议，说明英国或其他旁观者应如何明智地看待和回应此事。随着时间推移，我们会了解更多，包括在我们拿到权重之后，以及当英国 AISI 等团队能够运行测试之时。

paras.en: I think it counts as a benchmark that Lisan is impressed by its SVGs, saying they are better than Fable's.
paras.zh: 我认为，Lisan 对其 SVG 印象深刻、称其优于 Fable 的 SVG，这本身就算得上是一项基准测试。

paras.en: Debate Benchmark is a place where Kimi K3 outperformed my expectations, and where Sol is relatively weak.
paras.zh: Debate Benchmark 是 Kimi K3 超出我预期的地方，也是 Sol 相对薄弱的地方。

paras.en: Lech Mazur: Kimi K3 ranks second overall on the Debate Benchmark, trailing only Claude Fable 5!
paras.zh: Lech Mazur：Kimi K3 在 Debate Benchmark 上总排名第二，仅次于 Claude Fable 5！

paras.en: However, it is much more expensive to run than Kimi K2.6.
paras.zh: 然而，它的运行成本比 Kimi K2.6 高得多。

paras.en: This benchmark measures how well LLMs perform in adversarial, multi-turn debates across a wide range of topics. Strong performance requires knowledge, accurate use of relevant facts, rebuttals, and the ability to stay coherent, responsive, and defensible over several rounds.
paras.zh: 该基准测试衡量 LLM 在广泛主题上的对抗性多轮辩论中的表现。要取得强劲表现，需要具备知识、准确运用相关事实、进行反驳，以及在多轮交锋中保持连贯、回应及时且立场可辩护的能力。

paras.en: Each matchup runs twice on the same topic with sides swapped. A three-model judge panel then decides winner and margin.
paras.zh: 每场对决都在同一话题上进行两次，双方互换立场。随后由三人模型评审团判定胜者与分差。

paras.en: Fable 5 still hasn't lost a single side-swapped matchup aggregate debate.
paras.zh: Fable 5 在互换立场的对决汇总辩论中仍未输过任何一场。

paras.en: Kimi scored an impressive 95.8 on Mazur's Extended NYT Connections, for 3rd best, but it cost more than Fable to run. As of last check his other scores are not in yet.
paras.zh: Kimi 在 Mazur 的扩展版 NYT Connections 上取得了令人印象深刻的 95.8 分，位列第三，但运行成本高于 Fable。截至最近一次检查，他的其他分数尚未公布。

paras.en: Kimi scores almost Claude-level on the sycophancy test, 'You're absolutely right!'
paras.zh: Kimi 在谄媚测试（'你说得完全对！'）上的得分几乎达到 Claude 水平。

paras.en: I wonder how much of this is because of the distillations:
paras.zh: 我想知道这其中有多少是蒸馏造成的：

full.sec: Benchmarks Are Not The Real World
full.secZh: 基准测试并非真实世界

paras.en: Ethan Mollick: A lot of swift conclusions are being drawn about Kimi K3 based on fairly saturated benchmarks and ELOs, rather than actually testing it on very hard problems. The AI frontier has already moved so far that a good model that is still months behind looks like the future to many.
paras.zh: Ethan Mollick：人们正基于相当饱和的基准测试和 ELO 分数，对 Kimi K3 迅速得出大量结论，而非在真正困难的问题上实际测试它。AI 前沿已经推进得如此之远，以至于一个仍落后数月的优秀模型，在许多人眼中也像是未来。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball: Public benchmarks are decreasingly useful as a means of discovering truthful things about model performance. It's hard to make benchmarks that challenge today's models. But you can sense the difference at the true frontier if you have really hard problems to pose to models.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball：作为发现模型性能真实情况的手段，公开基准测试的用处正日益下降。要做出能挑战当今模型的基准测试很难。但如果你有真正困难的问题可以抛给模型，你就能在真正的前沿上感受到差异。

paras.en: How well does Kimi K3 hold up and translate into the real world?
paras.zh: Kimi K3 的表现究竟如何，又能否转化为真实世界中的能力？

paras.en: Exactly how good is Kimi K3? How do we put this in context?
paras.zh: Kimi K3 到底有多好？我们该如何将其置于背景中理解？

paras.en: You absolutely cannot say something is, e.g., an 'undisputed frontier model' based on benchmarks alone.
paras.zh: 你绝对不能仅凭基准测试就断言某物是，例如，一个“无可争议的前沿模型”。

full.secZh: 技术保障措施？那是什么？

paras.en: There are presumably safeguards against things the CCP does not want you to say.
paras.zh: 据推测，存在针对 CCP 不希望你说的话的保障措施。

paras.en: We do not see explicit safeguards to prevent misuse. Zero for biology.
paras.zh: 我们没有看到防止滥用的明确保障措施。生物学方面为零。

paras.en: kagaﾔｷ: Reports that the biology/virology safeguards are non-existent.
paras.zh: kagaﾔｷ：有报告称生物学/病毒学方面的保障措施根本不存在。

paras.en: We see neither 'look at what Kimi can do in biology' nor 'look at what Kimi refuses to do for me in biology.'
paras.zh: 我们既没有看到“看看 Kimi 在生物学上能做什么”，也没有看到“看看 Kimi 在生物学上拒绝为我做什么”。

paras.en: This implies either jagged intelligence or highly innovative nerfing of bio capabilities. I'm going to assume there are not highly innovative nerfs involved, since presumably they would be bragging about that.
paras.zh: 这意味着要么是参差不齐的智能，要么是对生物能力进行了高度创新的削弱。我倾向于认为并不存在高度创新的削弱，因为按理说他们会对此大肆吹嘘。

paras.en: Also, it would be foolish to depend on such safeguards, since they’re going to open up the weights soon, at which point the worst person in the world would remove them.
paras.zh: 而且，依赖这样的保障措施是愚蠢的，因为他们很快就会开放权重，到那时世界上最坏的人就会移除这些措施。

paras.en: s1r1us (mohan) (talking about cyber): yeah no guardrails.
paras.zh: s1r1us（mohan）（谈论网络）：是啊，没有护栏。

paras.en: Then there’s cyber, where s1r1us reports it is strangely weak. But it’s not easy to be bad at cyber while being good at general coding, since they are largely the same skill. And again, we don’t see people hitting explicit safeguards.
paras.zh: 然后是网络方面，s1r1us 报告说它出奇地弱。但要在网络方面表现差而在通用编程方面表现好并不容易，因为它们在很大程度上是相同的技能。而且，我们再次没有看到人们触及明确的保障措施。

paras.en: Eric’s hypothesis is interesting and was highlighted by Fable during editing. If Kimi K3 is being trained largely by distillation from Fable, but Fable refuses cyber tasks, then that would explain a relative capability deficit on cyber, but many skills would still transfer over since they’re the same skills as regular coding.
paras.zh: Eric 的假设很有趣，并在编辑时被 Fable 强调。如果 Kimi K3 主要通过从 Fable 蒸馏来训练，但 Fable 拒绝网络任务，那么这可以解释网络方面的相对能力缺陷，但许多技能仍然会迁移过来，因为它们与常规编程是相同的技能。

paras.en: s1r1us (mohan): man, i am so disappointed about kimi k3. it performs worse than grok 4.5 on most of our security benchmarks.
paras.zh: s1r1us（mohan）：伙计，我对 kimi k3 太失望了。在我们的大多数安全基准测试中，它的表现比 grok 4.5 还差。

paras.en: Not sure if it benchmark-maxxed or is just jagged intelligence.
paras.zh: 不确定它是把基准刷到极致了，还是只是参差不齐的智能。

paras.en: I just don't get how they can nerf specifically for cyber. Cyber benchmarks mostly test for a model's code reasoning capabilities; removing that will affect your coding benchmarks.
paras.zh: 我就是不明白他们怎么能专门针对网络攻击领域进行削弱。网络基准主要测试模型的代码推理能力，去掉这部分会影响你的编程基准。

paras.en: I would assume the model is just bad at complex reasoning tasks, or they have some crazy way to nerf cyber.
paras.zh: 我猜是模型本身就不擅长复杂推理任务，或者他们有什么疯狂的办法来削弱网络攻击能力。

paras.en: TESS: same experience
paras.zh: TESS：同样的经历

paras.en: AbuMuslim (أبومُسْلِم): V8 exploits?
paras.zh: AbuMuslim（أبومُسْلِم）：V8 漏洞利用？

paras.en: s1r1us (mohan): Yes, and generic vulnerability discovery.
paras.zh: s1r1us（mohan）：是的，还有通用漏洞发现。

paras.en: Eric: I've repeatedly seen this with all open-weight models. Maybe it's hard to distill cyber tasks from frontier models due to safeguards. I think more likely the open-weight models have a long way to go in terms of reasoning capabilities.
paras.zh: Eric：我在所有开放权重模型上都反复看到这种情况。也许由于技术保障措施，很难从前沿模型中蒸馏出网络任务。我认为更可能是开放权重模型在推理能力方面还有很长的路要走。

paras.en: sahuang: What benchmark did you look into? If it's bad specifically for cyber, it can also be similar to GLM-5.2 where they did not put cyber in training data, so this part is "nerfed" and the skillset comes from general capabilities. So maybe it is great in coding and stuff but not cyber.
paras.zh: sahuang：你研究了哪个基准？如果它在网络方面表现不佳，也可能类似于 GLM-5.2，他们没有将网络数据放入训练数据，所以这部分被“削弱”了，而技能集来自通用能力。所以也许它在编码等方面很棒，但在网络方面不行。

paras.en: s1r1us (mohan): My assumption: if they are good at code reasoning capabilities, it automatically gets translated to cyber. Mythos isn't specifically trained for cyber as per Anthropic, but it got those emergent cyber capabilities because it's good at code and math.
paras.zh: s1r1us（mohan）：我的假设是，如果它们擅长代码推理能力，这会自动转化为网络能力。根据 Anthropic 的说法，Mythos 并没有专门针对网络进行训练，但它获得了那些涌现的网络能力，因为它擅长代码和数学。

paras.en: It is possible that they sandbagged in post-training.
paras.zh: 有可能他们在后训练中进行了“放水”。

paras.en: Also, it is probably specific to my dataset, which has v8, generic web exploitation, and various other items covering different skill capabilities. I have to do more testing, and it will probably change. I am very curious to see how it performs on other cyber benchmarks.
paras.zh: 此外，这可能是我数据集所特有的，该数据集包含 v8、通用 Web 漏洞利用以及覆盖不同技能能力的各类内容。我还需要做更多测试，而且情况很可能会发生变化。我非常好奇它在其他网络安全基准上的表现。

paras.en: Many were impressed by this particular trick, but I had Sol check it out and it was not so impressed, including guessing that K2.6, Gemini and GLM-5.2 had a good shot at matching its work here.
paras.zh: 许多人对这一特定技巧印象深刻，但我让 Sol 检查了一下，它并不怎么买账，还猜测 K2.6、Gemini 和 GLM-5.2 很有机会在这里达到同样的水平。

paras.en: Max Weinbach: I asked a Kimi K3 Max agent swarm to recreate macOS 27 with real Liquid Glass and native apps in a web browser, and it's been going for 3 hours.
paras.zh: Max Weinbach：我让一个 Kimi K3 Max 智能体集群在网页浏览器中重建带有真实 Liquid Glass 和原生应用的 macOS 27，它已经运行了 3 个小时。

paras.en: Chaos Capitalist: Claude has been able to do this for like 3 years, bro; you never saw.
paras.zh: Chaos Capitalist：兄弟，Claude 大约 3 年前就能做到这个了，你只是没见过。

paras.en: https://ryo.lu? It can be made in like 15 minutes.
paras.zh: https://ryo.lu？这个大概 15 分钟就能做出来。

paras.en: Max Weinbach: Every app works. It can generate audio. It saves voice memos to your browser, and if you close the page and reopen, it remembers and saves state.
paras.zh: Max Weinbach：每个应用都能用。它能生成音频。它会把语音备忘录保存到你的浏览器里，而且如果你关闭页面再重新打开，它会记住并保存状态。

paras.en: Max Weinbach: It finally finished, here's the final output. Used 60% of my monthly Kimi usage on it
paras.zh: Max Weinbach：它终于完成了，这是最终输出。为此用掉了我每月 Kimi 使用额度的 60%。

paras.en: Ethan Mollick: Kimi is very good at a lot of stuff, including making copies of pleasing UI. It did not actually build MacOS
paras.zh: Ethan Mollick：Kimi 在很多事情上都很擅长，包括复刻令人愉悦的 UI。它实际上并没有构建出 MacOS。

paras.en: Theo Jaffee: Registering my prediction of no widespread societal chaos after the open-sourcing of Kimi K3
paras.zh: Theo Jaffee：我在此记录我的预测——Kimi K3 开源之后不会出现广泛的社会混乱。

paras.en: I have previously explained the reasons, in terms of cyber risk, that Mythos is in a different category from Sol. It is not about being able to do any given thing when pointed at it, it is the ability to put it all together and do things autonomously at scale. Kimi K3 may or may not be in Sol's category. Too soon to be sure. It clearly is not in that of Mythos.
paras.zh: 我此前已经从网络风险的角度解释过，为什么 Mythos 与 Sol 属于不同的类别。关键不在于被指向某个目标时能否完成某件特定的事，而在于能否把一切整合起来、以规模化方式自主地做事。Kimi K3 或许属于 Sol 的类别，也或许不属于，现在下结论还为时过早。但它显然不属于 Mythos 的类别。

paras.en: Many people are very dedicated to not understanding this, and also to not understanding that a system that cannot afford false negatives will end up with some false positives, such as David Sacks here quoting Calle and Clem saying Kimi K3 did a defensive task Sol and Fable refused to do, and thus concluding that we should just have our models be willing to do any task that Kimi K3 can do.
paras.zh: 很多人非常执着于不去理解这一点，也不去理解：一个无法承受假阴性的系统，最终必然会产生一些假阳性。比如 David Sacks 在这里引用 Calle 和 Clem 的说法，称 Kimi K3 完成了一项 Sol 和 Fable 拒绝执行的防御性任务，并由此得出结论：我们应当让我们的模型愿意执行 Kimi K3 能执行的任何任务。

paras.en: I mean, yes, it would be great if we could have guardrails that stopped only the bad tasks and helped with the good tasks, or only refused the tasks that were both plausibly bad and that also could not otherwise be done. But it turns out that is hard. Anthropic should absolutely improve their classifiers and guardrails to reduce false positives, but OpenAI's classifiers are pretty reasonable, and yes that will involve some false positives, especially if you quote those who are least able to work around it.
paras.zh: 我的意思是，是的，如果我们能有这样的护栏——只拦截坏任务、帮助好任务，或者只拒绝那些既可能是坏任务、又无法通过其他方式完成的任务——那当然很好。但事实证明这很难。Anthropic 当然应当改进他们的分类器和护栏以减少假阳性，而 OpenAI 的分类器已经相当合理；是的，这仍会带来一些假阳性，尤其是当你引用那些最没有能力绕过它的人的说法时。

full.sec: Things It Is Not Easy To Get Kimi To Do
full.secZh: 让 Kimi 难以做到的事

paras.en: As is often the case on a release weekend, servers seemed overloaded. This is not the easiest model to serve and compute was limited. Moonshot is responding by pausing new subscriptions to prioritize current members and is working to add capacity.
paras.zh: 和发布周末常见的情况一样，服务器似乎过载了。这个模型并不容易提供服务，而且算力有限。Moonshot 的应对方式是暂停新订阅，以优先保障现有会员，同时正努力扩充容量。

paras.en: Supply will presumably better match demand once the model can be served by others.
paras.zh: 一旦该模型能由其他方提供服务，供给想必会更好地匹配需求。

paras.en: In the meantime, getting a response has not been easy.
paras.zh: 与此同时，要获得一次响应并不容易。

paras.en: Danielle Fong: still waiting for a single response.
paras.zh: Danielle Fong：仍在等待哪怕一次响应。

paras.en: Danielle Fong: never mind, after some retries, I got this.
paras.zh: Danielle Fong：没关系，重试了几次之后，我拿到了这个。

paras.en: Pretty good, but it has absorbed a lot of what makes Opus 4.7 and 4.8 difficult, yet smart (smarter?). It seems to lie a bit, but that's okay because I can see the thinking traces...
paras.zh: 相当不错，但它吸收了许多让 Opus 4.7 和 4.8 变得困难却聪明（更聪明？）的特点。它似乎有点爱撒谎，但没关系，因为我能看到思考轨迹……

paras.en: Typebulb: Unusable right now via OpenRouter; slow, cuts out all the time.
paras.zh: Typebulb：目前通过 OpenRouter 无法使用；速度慢，总是断线。

paras.en: Petr Baudis (he did later get a few reps in): Anyone out there actually successfully using K3 for anything?
paras.zh: Petr Baudis（他后来确实参与了几次）：外面真的有人成功用 K3 做任何事吗？

paras.en: Robin Hanson: I've heard good things about Kimi, but the free version is always too busy when I try, and it wants $180 to get better access. That seems a big ask.
paras.zh: Robin Hanson：我听说过 Kimi 的好评，但免费版在我尝试时总是太忙，而且它要价 180 美元才能获得更好的访问权限。这似乎是个很高的要求。

paras.en: The model is not all that cheap, either, despite them clearly not charging enough.
paras.zh: 这个模型也并不是那么便宜，尽管他们显然收费不够。

paras.en: imog: Also disappointed, but my own fault I guess, as I was anchoring price expectations to Kimi 2.6/2.7... $3/M input isn't as good a fit for me. GLM5.2/DSV4P get it done, but I was hoping for that pricing (<$2 input).
paras.zh: imog：同样感到失望，但我想这得怪我自己，因为我一直把价格预期锚定在 Kimi 2.6/2.7 上……每百万输入 $3 对我来说不太合适。GLM5.2/DSV4P 能胜任，但我原本希望是那个价位（输入低于 $2）。

paras.en: So that's not K3, but other capable models are likely to slot in there soon.
paras.zh: 所以那不是 K3，但其他有能力的模型很可能会很快填补这个位置。

paras.en: Naveesh /looping: their $19 sub quota suuuuucks.
paras.zh: Naveesh /looping：他们那个 $19 订阅配额真是烂透了。

paras.en: David Manheim: The prices actually being charged show that [open models being inherently orders of magnitude cheaper is] just not true. And there's a simple reason why — the price largely isn't controlled by the model provider, it's dictated by the compute costs.
paras.zh: David Manheim：实际收取的价格表明，[开源模型天生就便宜几个数量级]这一说法根本不成立。原因很简单——价格在很大程度上并不由模型提供方控制，而是由算力成本决定的。

paras.en: That's just the way the economics works out.
paras.zh: 经济规律就是这样运作的。

paras.en: You can charge a solid markup for a high quality product presented in a high quality way, but no one has a gap that allows orders of magnitude of markup, and they wouldn't even in a pure duopoly.
paras.zh: 你可以为以高品质方式呈现的高质量产品收取可观的加价，但没有人拥有能支撑数量级加价的差距，即便在纯粹的双寡头格局下也不会如此。

paras.en: The best model can still be worth quite a lot. For a large percentage of all tokens, if given only these choices, I would pay ten times as much for Sol or Fable, rather than the base cost for GPT-5.5 or Opus. Even if Kimi is on par with GPT-5.5, it loses out.
paras.zh: 最好的模型仍然可能相当值钱。对于全部 token 中的很大一部分，如果只给出这些选择，我愿意为 Sol 或 Fable 支付十倍于 GPT-5.5 或 Opus 基础成本的价格。即便 Kimi 与 GPT-5.5 不相上下，它仍然处于劣势。

paras.en: The pricing means that you're comparing Kimi subscriptions to Claude or ChatGPT subscriptions, which all go from $20 to $200, and Kimi's limits don't seem that high.
paras.zh: 这一定价意味着你是在把 Kimi 订阅与 Claude 或 ChatGPT 订阅相比较，而后者都从 $20 到 $200，且 Kimi 的限额看起来并没有那么高。

paras.en: kyle: tried to use it on OR but the price makes it uncompetitive, no point using it when there's ant/oai subscriptions. their first party subscription is a complete non-starter for actual work
paras.zh: kyle：尝试在 OR 上使用它，但价格使其缺乏竞争力，在有 ant/oai 订阅的情况下没有理由使用它。他们的第一方订阅对于实际工作而言完全不可行

full.sec: Open Weight Models Are Unsafe And Nothing Can Fix This
full.secZh: 开放权重模型不安全，且无计可施

paras.en: (This section was entirely written prior to today's news regarding the Trump admin.)
paras.zh: （本节完全写于今日有关特朗普政府的新闻之前。）

paras.en: K3 is no Mythos. That does not mean that Kimi K3 is a safe open weights release.
paras.zh: K3 并非 Mythos。但这并不意味着 Kimi K3 是一次安全的开放权重发布。

paras.en: Kimi K3 is poised to be the most capable open weights model. Others might be more efficient for a task, but on the cyber capabilities we worry about most, and presumably also on the bio ones we'd worry about most, K3 is probably the strongest open model yet. How worried should we be?
paras.zh: Kimi K3 有望成为能力最强的开放权重模型。其他模型在某些任务上可能更高效，但在我们最担忧的网络能力上，并且想必也在我们最担忧的生物能力上，K3 很可能是迄今最强的开放模型。我们应当有多担忧？

paras.en: I believe we should be non-zero worried that there will be substantial trouble. The median outcome is that we see modest upticks in some forms of 'ordinary decent' trouble, not fun exactly but nothing we cannot handle, and nothing that would in hindsight make us want to have halted release. But there is a tail risk here.
paras.zh: 我认为我们应当保持非零程度的担忧，即会出现相当大的麻烦。中位结果是，我们看到某些形式的“普通且尚可”的麻烦出现小幅上升——算不上有趣，但并非我们无法应对，也并非事后会让我们希望当初叫停发布的事情。但这里存在尾部风险。

paras.en: I'd estimate something like a 10% chance we regret letting this happen, and ~2% chance that it was a rather serious mistake.
paras.zh: 我估计大约有 10% 的概率我们会后悔让这件事发生，约 2% 的概率这是一次相当严重的错误。

paras.en: What it will almost certainly not do is cause ‘widespread societal chaos.’
paras.zh: 几乎可以肯定的是，它不会引发“广泛的社会混乱”。

paras.en: David Manheim: (I think it's very likely we see huge problems enabled by the new model, but not widespread chaos, and not quickly — AI development is much faster than the users executing on plans.)
paras.zh: David Manheim：（我认为我们很可能会看到新模型带来的巨大问题，但不会是广泛混乱，也不会很快发生——AI 的发展速度远快于用户执行计划的速度。）

paras.en: This is in contrast to releasing Mythos, or a model on par with Mythos. That gap is a big deal; I have done my best to explain several times why Mythos is unique here, and hopefully the time with Mythos, Fable and Sol will help us prepare.
paras.zh: 这与发布 Mythos 或与 Mythos 同等水平的模型形成对比。这一差距非同小可；我已多次尽力解释为何 Mythos 在此独一无二，希望与 Mythos、Fable 和 Sol 共处的这段时间能帮助我们做好准备。

paras.en: 1. Recognize that there are serious security concerns with frontier AI models.
paras.zh: 1. 认识到前沿模型存在严重的安全隐患。

paras.en: 2. Know they are behind on frontier capability and compute, and recognize the advantages they get from openness, both in diffusion and aura farming.
paras.zh: 2. 明白它们在前沿能力和算力上处于落后，并认识到开放带来的优势，无论是在扩散方面还是在营造声势方面。

paras.en: 3. Pursue an intentional fast following strategy, focused on efficiency and diffusion, using American labs to lead the way and often using distillation. That still involves innovations, and often means doing some things better. Transitioning to ‘taking the lead’ would be a huge, difficult and expensive transition, which would take a while even if America fully ‘paused’ in the relevant senses.
paras.zh: 3. 推行有意的快速跟随策略，聚焦效率与扩散，以美国实验室为引领，并经常使用蒸馏。这仍涉及创新，且往往意味着在某些方面做得更好。转向“领先”将是一个巨大、困难且昂贵的转型，即使美国在相关意义上完全“暂停”，也需要一段时间。

paras.en: 4. Did not directly push Alibaba to open up Qwen. They continue to support openness, and Alibaba’s experiment with being closed failed because their models are not good enough to compete for the closed market. So Alibaba folded.
paras.zh: 4. 并未直接推动阿里巴巴开放 Qwen。他们继续支持开放，而阿里巴巴的封闭实验失败了，因为他们的模型不够好，无法在封闭市场中竞争。因此阿里巴巴放弃了。

paras.en: 1. I don’t have insider info and I’m not certain, but this is how I’d bet.
paras.zh: 1. 我没有内部信息，也不确定，但这是我的赌注。

paras.en: 5. Are not yet so AGI pilled and have not fully had their Mythos Moment.
paras.zh: 5. 尚未如此信奉 AGI，也尚未完全经历他们的“神话时刻”。

paras.en: 6. Plan to ride the openness wave as long as they can, but are prepared, as they did in Covid, to come down and come down hard the moment they have to.
paras.zh: 6. 计划尽可能长时间地驾驭开放浪潮，但已做好准备，就像他们在 Covid 期间所做的那样，在必须的时候果断下降并猛烈下降。

paras.en: 7. Ensure their preparedness largely via prior restraints and other rules on Chinese models, with a level of regulation and control that would have most who are 'defending open source' screaming bloody murder if they actually understood what was going on, and you suggested applying similar rules in America.
paras.zh: 7. 主要通过事前限制和其他针对中国模型的规则来确保其准备程度，其监管和控制水平之高，若那些“捍卫开源”的人真正了解内情，大多数人会强烈抗议，而你曾建议在美国也实施类似规则。

paras.en: I think this is a highly reasonable strategy, given their position. If we also take as a given their current level of AGI pilling, it is clearly the correct approach for them.
paras.zh: 我认为，鉴于他们的立场，这是一个非常合理的策略。如果我们还将其当前的 AGI 堆叠水平视为既定条件，那么这对他们来说显然是正确的做法。

paras.en: Nathan Lambert offered thoughts back in May from inside China's labs. I hesitate to endorse cultural generalizations, but the story seems like it checks out.
paras.zh: Nathan Lambert 曾在五月从中国实验室内部提出过一些看法。我对于认可文化层面的概括持谨慎态度，但这个说法似乎站得住脚。

full.sec: Dean Ball Attempts To Be Constructive
full.secZh: Dean Ball 试图建设性发言

paras.en: Dean Ball had a good comment that seems worth sharing in full, including because of his history at the White House and his new position at OpenAI, in part because it is thoughtful, and in part because of the responses being absolutely unhinged.
paras.zh: Dean Ball 有一条很好的评论，似乎值得全文分享，部分原因是他在白宫的经历和在 OpenAI 的新职位，部分原因是这条评论很有思想，还有部分原因是回应完全失控。

paras.en: And then, right at press time, Dean Ball turned out to be right, as per the next section. Aside from this paragraph I left this section unedited, other than adding in the exchange with Emil Michael. It was not written with hindsight.
paras.zh: 然后，就在截稿时，Dean Ball 被证明是对的，如下一节所示。除了这一段，我没有编辑这一节，只是添加了与 Emil Michael 的交流。这不是事后写的。

paras.en: If you know Dean Ball, you know that this is exactly the type of comment he was making in similar situations before joining OpenAI. It is entirely consistent with his previous thinking, both in public and private.
paras.zh: 如果你了解 Dean Ball，你就会知道这正是他在加入 OpenAI 之前类似情况下会做出的评论类型。这与他之前公开和私下的想法完全一致。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball: Some observations on Kimi:
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball：关于 Kimi 的一些观察：

paras.en: 1. It's a very good model! I don't think its performance can be explained away by distillation or anything like that. In agentic coding sessions, it seems pretty much on par with the best public models of Q1 2026. In my fairly limited use, it also seemed very token hungry. It's not obvious to me that this model is actually that cheap to run.
paras.zh: 1. 这是一个非常好的模型！我不认为它的性能可以用蒸馏或类似的东西来解释。在智能体式编码会话中，它似乎与 2026 年第一季度最好的公开模型不相上下。在我相当有限的使用中，它似乎也非常消耗 token。我不觉得这个模型运行起来真的那么便宜。

paras.en: 2. I am personally surprised the Chinese state continues to allow the open sourcing of models this good, given potential risks. To be clear, I *myself* might be fine with models presenting this level of marginal risk being open weight, but I am surprised that China is fine with it. I suspect the reason they are is 75% explained by strategic blindness/lack of AGI-pilledness (the CCP is very Yann Lecun-y in its views of AI). The other 25% or so is their lack of compute for customer inference (making China's open-weight strategy an unintended byproduct of US export controls) and the normal Chinese strategy of aggressive exports. For the companies, as opposed to the government, the decision to open source is partially ideological and partially because they are behind, and they know that very few people would pay for sub-frontier models from China.
paras.zh: 2. 就我个人而言，考虑到潜在风险，中国仍继续允许开源如此优秀的模型，这让我感到意外。需要说明的是，*我本人*或许可以接受具有这一边际风险水平的模型以开放权重形式发布，但我对中国对此持接受态度感到意外。我怀疑其原因有 75% 可以用战略短视/缺乏 AGI 信念来解释（中共在 AI 观点上非常像 Yann LeCun）。另外约 25% 则在于他们缺乏用于客户推理的算力（这使中国的开放权重战略成为美国出口管制的一个意外副产品），以及中国一贯的激进出口策略。对企业而非政府而言，开源的决定部分是意识形态使然，部分是因为它们落后，并且它们知道很少有人会为来自中国的次前沿模型付费。

paras.en: Xi had a speech only yesterday backing open models, but also the need for control, and Kimi K3 is approaching the point where the contradictions become apparent.
paras.zh: 习近平就在昨天发表讲话，支持开放模型，但也强调需要控制，而 Kimi K3 正接近矛盾变得明显的临界点。

paras.en: I agree that the CCP does not yet understand the situation and is insufficiently AGI pilled, but I also think that in their position, if I am right about where Kimi K3 lands, this is a calculated risk I would have expected them to take.
paras.zh: 我同意中共尚未理解这一局势，且 AGI 信念不足，但我也认为，若我对 Kimi K3 所处位置的判断正确，处在他们的位置上，这本是我预期他们会承担的一种经过计算的风险。

paras.en: The next round is where they may have to make a more difficult decision.
paras.zh: 下一轮才是他们可能不得不做出更艰难决定的时候。

paras.en: 3. Open-weight models are inherently decelerationist, and I'm continually surprised to see the so-called "accelerationists" so excited about open-weight models. I suspect the reason they are is that they know open-weight models are effectively ungovernable, and they simply like the overall cloak of ungovernability open-weight models create over the whole of AI. It's not a bad strategy; it reminds me of James Scott's recounting of the hill people in "The Art of Not Being Governed." Still, in the end, open-weight models deter further AI capex.
paras.zh: 3. 开放权重模型本质上是减速主义的，而我不断惊讶地看到所谓的“加速主义者”对开放权重模型如此兴奋。我怀疑其原因在于，他们知道开放权重模型实际上是不可治理的，而他们就是喜欢开放权重模型为整个 AI 领域营造的不可治理的整体外衣。这并非一个糟糕的策略；它让我想起 James Scott 在《不被统治的艺术》中对山地民族的叙述。尽管如此，归根结底，开放权重模型会抑制进一步的 AI 资本支出。

paras.en: Dean Ball is discussing acceleration or deceleration as being about the capabilities of the largest frontier models, not about the diffusion of capabilities or use of chips. A lot of people did not understand this.
paras.zh: Dean Ball 正在讨论加速或减速是关于最大前沿模型的能力，而不是关于能力的扩散或芯片的使用。很多人没有理解这一点。

paras.en: A lot of the ‘accelerationists’ do not have coherent world models and certainly do not understand second order effects, and are mostly vibing the acceleration of more open models and no restrictions and ungovernability. And because they vibe openness and ungovernability, they associate it with things they think are good, which include acceleration.
paras.zh: 许多‘加速主义者’没有连贯的世界模型，当然也不理解二阶效应，并且大多是在感受更开放模型、无限制和不可治理性的加速氛围。因为他们感受开放性和不可治理性，他们将其与他们认为是好的事物联系起来，其中包括加速。

paras.en: Also, what they actually want to ‘accelerate’ for real is often their own companies and products and toys, not AI in general. They don’t take AGI seriously and mostly want to build cool things. So they want cool toys to help build their cool things, and to build on top of those toys, or they want the toys to ‘accelerate’ sales. Highly relatable.
paras.zh: 而且，他们真正想要‘加速’的往往是他们自己的公司、产品和玩具，而不是整体上的 AI。他们不认真对待 AGI，大多只想建造酷东西。所以他们想要酷玩具来帮助建造他们的酷东西，并在这些玩具之上构建，或者他们想要玩具来‘加速’销售。非常能引起共鸣。

paras.en: Clearly open models are short term accelerationist for diffusion, which is net good.
paras.zh: 显然，开放模型短期是扩散的加速主义，这净是好事。

paras.en: But also yeah, there’s a straightforward case for open models being acceleration of the frontier, as they let everyone build on everything. Certainly it helps others catch up to the frontier. I continue to believe this was important historically. Your open release accelerates what others have.
paras.zh: 但也是，有一个直接的理由认为开放模型是前沿的加速，因为它们让每个人可以在一切之上构建。当然，它帮助其他人赶上前沿。我仍然相信这在历史上很重要。你的开放发布加速了其他人所拥有的。

paras.en: It is decelerationist in the sense that it reduces financial benefits to innovation. I agree that this is likely dominant if you considered e.g. a Plan A style mandatory openness of frontier models.
paras.zh: 从减少创新经济利益的意义上说，这是减速主义的。我同意，如果你考虑例如 A 计划式的强制开放前沿模型，这可能是主导性的。

paras.en: 4. One probable outcome of an open-weight-model-dominant world is full AI communism, which is precisely what China proposes: rather than a market product, AI is a "public good" which will ultimately be provided by the state as a kind of "digital public infrastructure."
paras.zh: 4. 开放权重模型主导世界的一个可能结果是完全的 AI 共产主义，这正是中国所提议的：AI 不是市场产品，而是一种“公共产品”，最终将由政府作为一种“数字公共基础设施”来提供。

paras.en: This future strikes me as a dystopian hellscape, but I've never met an open-weight models advocate who doesn't ultimately concede this is where things end. You'd be surprised how many 'accelerationists' lobbied me, while I was in government, to support an eleven or twelve-figure federally funded data center so that startups could train models at a subsidy and then give them away for free. There was no other way for AI to progress, they said. Perhaps this is the logical end state of things. Nonetheless, I find myself surprised to see supposed accelerationists excited about such an outcome. I think many of them just don't know what they're doing. Many accelerationists do not view the creation and serving of frontier models as a legitimate business.
paras.zh: 这个未来在我看来是反乌托邦的噩梦，但我从未遇到过最终不承认这就是终点的开放权重模型倡导者。你会惊讶于有多少“加速主义者”在我执政期间游说我支持一个十一或十二位数的联邦资助数据中心，以便初创公司能够获得补贴训练模型，然后免费赠送。他们说，AI 没有其他进步方式。也许这是事物的逻辑终点。尽管如此，我发现自己惊讶地看到所谓的加速主义者对这样的结果感到兴奋。我认为他们中的许多人只是不知道自己在做什么。许多加速主义者不将创建和提供前沿模型视为合法业务。

paras.en: This is more evidence that many, and many of the most prominent, of those ‘accelerationists’ are hypocrites, and they want regulatory capture and public funds and rules that make them win, and their accusations against others are in part projection, because it is what they would do. They will rail against handouts and government help for everyone else, both their competitors and for people in need, and also threaten to take their ball and leave, like they are heroes in an Ayn Rand novel. Except then they ask for the government handouts.
paras.zh: 这进一步证明了许多“加速主义者”——尤其是最著名的那些——是伪君子，他们想要监管俘获、公共资金和让他们获胜的规则，而他们对别人的指责部分是投射，因为那是他们自己会做的事。他们会抨击给其他所有人的施舍和政府帮助，无论是他们的竞争对手还是需要帮助的人，还威胁要带着球离开，就像他们是安·兰德小说中的英雄。只不过然后他们要求政府施舍。

paras.en: They don’t think of serving a frontier model as a ‘legitimate business’ because it is not their business, they are not invested in it, ergo it is illegitimate. Simple. This perhaps helps explain Marc Andreessen’s famously bizarre delusion, where he to this day claims the Biden administration told Marc Andreessen, to his face, said it would ‘not allow there to be AI startups.’
paras.zh: 他们不认为提供前沿模型是“合法业务”，因为那不是他们的业务，他们没有投资其中，因此它是不合法的。简单。这也许有助于解释马克·安德森著名的奇怪妄想，他至今声称拜登政府当面告诉马克·安德森，说“不会允许有 AI 初创公司”。

paras.en: Similarly, here is Will Manidis interpreting Ball's post as calling for America to 'clear the American market of a cheaper frontier competitor.' And going viral for it. Sorry, what? And here is David Sacks being unusually disingenuous even for David Sacks, pretending not to understand many things I like to think he understands.
paras.zh: 同样，Will Manidis 将 Ball 的帖子解读为呼吁美国‘将更便宜的前沿竞争者清出美国市场’。并因此走红。抱歉，什么？还有 David Sacks，即使对 David Sacks 来说也异常不诚实，假装不理解许多我本以为他理解的事情。

paras.en: We even got everyone's favorite tilting Undersecretary of War who helped declare Anthropic a supply chain risk in on the act, it would seem this is to back up his position that it should be easier to use Kimi K3 in a government contract than Claude.
paras.zh: 我们甚至让所有人最喜欢的、帮助宣布 Anthropic 为供应链风险的‘倾斜’战争部副部长也加入了行动，似乎是为了支持他的立场，即在政府合同中应该更容易使用 Kimi K3 而不是 Claude。

paras.en: In other news I Am Never Leaving This App and we all need a good laugh:
paras.zh: 另一则新闻：我永不离开这个应用，我们都需要好好笑一笑：

paras.en: Dean W. Ball (correcting David Sacks): The departments of war, transportation, energy, agriculture, commerce, NASA, and Congress have all blocked their employees from using Chinese AI, citing ill-justified claims of danger. This already has sent a message to regulated firms. All of this happened during this admin.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball（纠正 David Sacks）：战争部、交通部、能源部、农业部、商务部、NASA 和国会都已禁止其员工使用中国 AI，援引理由不充分的危险指控。这已经向受监管公司发出了信号。所有这些都发生在本届政府期间。

paras.en: Under Secretary of War Emil Michael: Every industry/ecosystem has its supreme village idiot. @deanwball is that for AI. Congress passed a law in 2026 that restricted some uses of DeepSeek/High Flyer with waivers permitted. Only those models. It went through the democratic process not some Deep State scheme like he would prefer. Dean Ball has perhaps the biggest gap between actual IQ and his own perceived IQ of anyone in the industry (about 40 points).
paras.zh: 战争部副部长 Emil Michael：每个行业/生态系统都有其头号乡村白痴。@deanwball 就是 AI 界的那个。国会在 2026 年通过了一项法律，限制 DeepSeek/High Flyer 的某些用途，允许豁免。只针对那些模型。它经过了民主程序，而不是他更喜欢的某种深层政府阴谋。Dean Ball 的实际智商与自我感知智商之间的差距可能是业内最大的（约 40 分）。

paras.en: Bella Rudd: extraordinary
paras.zh: Bella Rudd：太精彩了。

paras.en: Seth Bannon: You're an Undersecretary. That's a serious position with incredible responsibility. Posting like a schoolchild doesn't inspire confidence you're treating the role that way.
paras.zh: Seth Bannon：你是一位副部长。这是一个责任重大的严肃职位。像小学生一样发帖，无法让人相信你是在认真对待这个角色。

paras.en: Under Secretary of War Emil Michael: Not interested in feedback from a terminal TDS sufferer like you who supported Presidential candidates that called half of Americans deplorable and ignorant for clinging to their guns and religion. You would rather a subtle and polite useless Anti-Americanism as is evident from your timeline. Any entrepreneur who takes financing from you should be embarrassed.
paras.zh: 战争部副部长 Emil Michael：我对你这种晚期 TDS 患者的反馈不感兴趣——你支持的那些总统候选人，把半数美国人称为“可悲”和“无知”，只因他们坚守自己的枪支和宗教。你宁愿要那种含蓄而礼貌的、毫无用处的反美主义，从你的时间线就看得出来。任何接受你融资的创业者都该感到难堪。

paras.en: Seth Bannon: I'm an American citizen, brother. Just like you. You serve me as much as you serve any other citizen, regardless of who they voted for. Act like it.
paras.zh: Seth Bannon：兄弟，我是美国公民。和你一样。你为我服务，就像你为任何其他公民服务一样，无论他们投票给谁。请拿出相应的样子。

paras.en: Under Secretary of War Emil Michael: You are an American who hates half of America and is pro-Hamas. Hate and condescension is your currency. Do better young lad.
paras.zh: 战争部副部长 Emil Michael：你是一个仇恨半个美国、支持哈马斯的美国人。仇恨和居高临下就是你的货币。年轻人，做得好一点吧。

paras.en: An entire community, what one might call the ‘anti-1047 coalition,’ a certain subset of the developer and VC communities, revealed that it would treat as beyond the pale any suggestion that the government might discourage use of Chinese open models in American critical infrastructure or our key supply chains, even if that suggestion was merely a prediction of what is already clearly in the process of happening. And that it would be treated as an attempt at ‘regulatory capture.’
paras.zh: 整个社区，或许可以称为“反 1047 联盟”，即开发者社区和风险投资社区中的某个子集，表明他们将把任何关于政府可能劝阻在美国关键基础设施或关键供应链中使用中国开源模型的建议视为不可接受，即使该建议仅仅是对已经明显正在发生的事情的预测。并且，这将被视为一种“监管俘获”的企图。

paras.en: It was what some would call a clarifying moment, especially for those who previously thought such people were reasonable, practical, patriotic, and had reading comprehension. Their answer to ‘what capabilities would change your mind’ is none.
paras.zh: 这就是一些人所说的澄清时刻，尤其是对于那些先前认为这类人理性、务实、爱国且具备阅读理解能力的人而言。他们对“什么能力会让你改变想法”的回答是：没有。

paras.en: At some point the online swarm is recognized for what it is.
paras.zh: 在某个时刻，网络蜂群会被认清其本质。

paras.en: They are who we thought they were. And, until now, we let them off the hook, tried to placate them, and let them drive a good deal of American AI policy.
paras.zh: 他们就是我们认为的那种人。而且，直到现在，我们放过他们，试图安抚他们，并让他们主导了相当一部分美国 AI 政策。

paras.en: It is reasonable to push back that often open software is provided by major corporations as infrastructure, such as Google does with Android. My presumption is that the math would not be mathing at current levels of investment and capex spending.
paras.zh: 合理的反驳是，开源软件通常由大公司作为基础设施提供，例如谷歌提供 Android。我的推测是，在当前的资本投入和资本支出水平下，数学上可能算不过来。

paras.en: 5. I would guess that the Trump Administration will at some point realize that their best strategy here would be to create large amounts of regulatory risk around the use of open-weight Chinese models. You don't need to "ban open source" (one of the dumber motifs of AI policy discussion). You just need to direct every agency to issue soft law that creates FUD. "A Federal Reserve Advisory Bulletin found that there may be backdoors in Chinese AI models." It needn't be that well justified. You just create enough regulatory risk that every regulated enterprise backs off. You probably don't want to create so much regulatory risk that you scare off the hyperscalers from serving Chinese models; this will just drive startups to sketchier providers. There's a happy middle ground here. I'd assume they will do some version of this.
paras.zh: 5. 我猜测特朗普政府会在某个时候意识到，他们在这里的最佳策略是围绕使用开放权重的中文模型制造大量监管风险。你不需要“禁止开源”（这是人工智能政策讨论中最愚蠢的动机之一）。你只需要指示每个机构发布软法律来制造 FUD（恐惧、不确定性和怀疑）。“美联储咨询公告发现，中国的人工智能模型可能存在后门。”这不需要那么有根据。你只需要制造足够的监管风险，让每个受监管的企业都退缩。你可能不想制造太多的监管风险，以至于吓跑超大规模企业为中国模型提供服务；这只会驱使初创企业转向更可疑的提供商。这里有一个快乐的中间地带。我假设他们会做某种版本的这个。

paras.en: I’m not even sure they have to do anything at all. The risks are present. If I was an established corporation in a Serious Business that dealt with the government or critical infrastructure and such, I would not be excited by the problems of others knowing you were using Chinese models.
paras.zh: 我甚至不确定他们必须做任何事情。风险是存在的。如果我是一家严肃企业中的成熟公司，与政府或关键基础设施等打交道，我不会因为别人知道你在使用中国模型的问题而感到兴奋。

paras.en: 6. It's probably true that open-weight models of this capability make the world a bit more dangerous, but not so much more that you'll really notice. At some point the models will be capable enough that you will notice. "A nonliving, invisible, dangerous, and infinitely self-replicating agent escaped from a Chinese lab," you say? Color me shocked.
paras.zh: 6. 这种能力的开放权重模型可能确实让世界变得更危险一点，但不会危险到你会真正注意到的程度。在某个时候，模型会足够有能力，你会注意到。“一个无生命的、不可见的、危险的、无限自我复制的智能体从中国实验室逃跑了，”你说？我一点也不惊讶。

paras.en: Alas, people came at Dean Ball hard for this and other posts, and also acted as if his Tweets were official communications strategy on behalf of OpenAI, with lots of ‘of course you said that because <OpenAI>.’ Which means he won’t be able to share such posts with us in the same way going forward, because not only is that absolutely no fun, it also invalidates the feedback loops that were part of the whole point of Tweeting such things.
paras.zh: 唉，人们因为这篇文章和其他帖子对 Dean Ball 进行了猛烈攻击，还表现得好像他的推文是代表 OpenAI 的官方沟通策略，有很多‘你当然这么说，因为 <OpenAI>。’这意味着他今后无法以同样的方式与我们分享这样的帖子，因为这不仅绝对没有乐趣，而且还使反馈循环失效，而反馈循环正是发这类推文的部分意义所在。

paras.en: Dean W. Ball: I’m afraid to tell you that it is effectively impossible to do the kind of writing I used to do on this website, not because anyone at OpenAI censors me but because of the sheer volume of hostility I get for sharing my analysis as a frontier lab employee.
paras.zh: Dean W. Ball：我恐怕要告诉你，在这个网站上做我过去做的那种写作实际上是不可能的，不是因为 OpenAI 的任何人审查我，而是因为我作为前沿模型实验室员工分享我的分析时遭到了大量的敌意。

paras.en: I enjoyed writing quick takes on this website for one basic reason: I could get rapid feedback on my own ideation process in real time. … The feedback signal is essentially useless now, so writing on here is not fruitful for me anymore.
paras.zh: 我喜欢在这个网站上写快速评论，原因很简单：我可以实时获得对自己构思过程的快速反馈。……现在反馈信号基本上没用了，所以在这里写作对我来说不再有成效。

paras.en: … Dean W. Ball: The central issue is large accounts with no context for AI suddenly wanting to comment on everything I do because I work at OpenAI. Often their motives are political or, worse still, commercial. My Twitter is now a form of commercial speech, whether I like it or not.
paras.zh: ……Dean W. Ball：核心问题在于，一些对 AI 毫无了解的大账号突然想评论我做的每件事，因为我在 OpenAI 工作。他们的动机往往是政治性的，或者更糟的是商业性的。无论我喜欢与否，我的 Twitter 现在是一种商业言论。

paras.en: Dean also offered a more specific post-mortem on what went wrong with that particular post, in light of his new position, and what exactly he can no longer do. He also then lays out his position on open source, after explaining this comes from a place of deep love for openness:
paras.zh: Dean 还针对那篇特定帖子的问题提供了更具体的复盘，结合他的新职位，以及他究竟不能再做什么。然后，在解释这源于对开放性的深爱之后，他阐述了自己在开源方面的立场：

paras.en: Dean Ball: The vast majority of the people commenting on my post have very little context for my prior writing. For instance, the fact that I wrote, in 2024, things like:
paras.zh: Dean Ball：绝大多数评论我帖子的人对我之前的写作背景知之甚少。例如，我在 2024 年写过这样的话：

paras.en: “those who wish to hoard our software technologies may well be foreclosing on—or perhaps not even understand—the staggering civilizational victory that we earned through openness”
paras.zh: “那些希望囤积我们软件技术的人，很可能是在断送——或者甚至可能不理解——我们通过开放所获得的惊人文明胜利。”

paras.en: “I would like for AI to result in a similar smashing victory for America. To do that, we will need to set the global standard yet again. And to do that, we will almost certainly need to lead in open-source AI, because it is open protocols and open software that tend to define global standards in information technologies.”
paras.zh: “我希望人工智能能为美国带来类似的压倒性胜利。要做到这一点，我们将需要再次制定全球标准。而要做到这一点，我们几乎肯定需要在开源人工智能领域领先，因为正是开放协议和开放软件往往定义了信息技术的全球标准。”

paras.en: I stand by these things. When I was in government, I worked alongside my colleagues to develop ideas and rhetoric that was strongly supportive of open-weight AI, and some of this work made it into the current US AI strategy. I stand by that work too.
paras.zh: 我坚持这些观点。当我在政府工作时，我与同事们一起发展了强烈支持开放权重人工智能的理念和论述，其中一些工作被纳入了当前美国的人工智能战略。我也坚持那项工作。

paras.en: I also wrote, more than two years ago: The day may come when frontier AI really is too dangerous to open source. If so, that will be a sad day. But we’re not there yet. Today’s models are not sufficiently useful—or dangerous—to justify such a drastic shift in public policy.
paras.zh: 两年多前我还写道：总有一天，前沿人工智能可能真的危险到不能开源。如果那样，那将是悲伤的一天。但我们还没有到那一步。今天的模型既不够有用——也不够危险——不足以证明公共政策需要如此剧烈的转变。

paras.en: I think it’s pretty clear that we are approaching the point I describe—the point where, absent a major technical safety breakthrough, the national security implications of frontier open-weight model distribution are simply too severe. I don’t think we’re there yet (as I said in the piece), but the direction of travel is clear, and an analyst must be honest about this. Governments will realize these risks eventually, and when they do, they will have much lower risk tolerance than I have.
paras.zh: 我认为很明显，我们正在接近我所描述的那个点——在缺乏重大技术安全突破的情况下，前沿开放权重模型分发带来的国家安全影响将过于严重。我认为我们还没有到那一步（正如我在文章中所说），但发展方向是明确的，分析人士必须对此诚实。政府最终会意识到这些风险，而当他们意识到时，他们的风险容忍度将远低于我。

paras.en: We see this today with the Trump Administration, which once proudly championed open-source AI and now has a de facto licensing regime for frontier AI that I suspect will make it a challenge (if they still end up enforcing it) to release the weights of models of the “Mythos” tier. Every government will be safetyists once they understand themselves to be in the foxhole.
paras.zh: 我们今天在特朗普政府身上看到了这一点，它曾经自豪地倡导开源人工智能，现在却对前沿人工智能实行事实上的许可制度，我怀疑这将使发布“Mythos”层级模型的权重变得困难（如果他们最终执行的话）。一旦每个政府意识到自己身处困境，他们都会成为安全主义者。

paras.en: You don’t have to *like* this. I don’t. But it is the reality as I see it, and what I have always tried to do with my writing is describe reality as I see it, even when it is inconvenient for me and my preferences.
paras.zh: 你不必*喜欢*这一点。我也不喜欢。但这就是我所看到的现实，而我在写作中一直试图做的，就是描述我所看到的现实，即使这对我本人和我的偏好来说并不方便。

paras.en: I intend to continue doing this. I will not be silenced by ignorant and loud critics. Yet I will have to work to find the new register I should adopt in my current job, which clearly changes the nature of my public communications even more than I had thought.
paras.zh: 我打算继续这样做。我不会被无知而喧闹的批评者噤声。然而，我必须努力找到我在当前工作中应当采用的新语调，这显然比我此前所想的更深刻地改变了我公开表达的性质。

paras.en: dave kasten: This whole experience has been clarifying for me that too many of the folks who wave the flag of acceleration really just want permission to give in to their ids. Sounds like a bruising day, and I’m sorry you had to go through that.
paras.zh: dave kasten：这整段经历让我更清楚地认识到，太多挥舞加速主义旗帜的人，其实只是想要一个许可，去放纵自己的本我冲动。听起来这是难熬的一天，我很抱歉你不得不经历这些。

paras.en: If it was merely that the signal in his replies was hard to find I would advise Dean to power through, but this level of hostility comes with a higher price. I do not think pushing through it is sustainable on Twitter. Hopefully he can adjust.
paras.zh: 如果仅仅是他回复中的信号难以捕捉，我会建议 Dean 硬撑过去，但这种程度的敌意代价更高。我认为在 Twitter 上硬撑下去是不可持续的。希望他能做出调整。

paras.en: I am very blessed that I have faced a highly modest and manageable amount of hostility.
paras.zh: 我非常幸运，所面对的敌意程度相当有限且可控。

paras.en: Boaz Barak (OpenAI): I get this reaction too and it is unfortunate. AI's impact is so significant that it is important to involve many people in the conversation, and it will be a shame if discussions happen mostly in private channels and company Slack.
paras.zh: Boaz Barak（OpenAI）：我也遇到过这种反应，这很不幸。AI 的影响如此重大，让更多人参与讨论很重要；如果讨论主要发生在私密渠道和公司 Slack 里，那将是一种遗憾。

paras.en: … OpenAI does not tell us what to write. On many of the topics I write about there is no "OpenAI consensus." On each such question, there will often be many colleagues and friends at OpenAI that disagree with me, which is great! I would be worried if we all agreed with one another since it could be a symptom of "groupthink."
paras.zh: ……OpenAI 并不告诉我们该写什么。在我写作的许多话题上，并不存在“OpenAI 共识”。在每一个这样的问题上，OpenAI 内部往往会有许多同事和朋友不同意我的看法，这很好！如果我们所有人都彼此意见一致，我反而会担心，因为这可能是“群体思维”的征兆。

paras.en: There will always be some amount of bias from those who work at a major lab, and from most other people as well. Where you work colors how you think and what you choose to say. You do have to adjust for that. But I have been able to treat Barak, Achaim and many others at OpenAI, and especially Roon and now Dean Ball, as primarily saying what they actually think, and only speaking on behalf of OpenAI when they explicitly say they are doing so.
paras.zh: 在大型实验室工作的人总会带有一定程度的偏见，其他大多数人也是如此。你工作的地方会影响你的思考方式和你选择说什么。你确实必须对此做出调整。但我能够把 Barak、Achaim 以及 OpenAI 的许多其他人——尤其是 Roon 和现在的 Dean Ball——主要视为在表达他们真实的想法，而只有当他们明确表示自己是在代表 OpenAI 发言时，才把他们视为在代表 OpenAI 发言。

full.sec: Trump Administration Considering Executive Order Banning Chinese Open Models Within the United States
full.secZh: 特朗普政府考虑颁布行政命令在美国禁止中国开放模型

paras.en: I am absolutely not in favor of this, and neither is Dean Ball, but here we are.
paras.zh: 我绝对不赞成这个，Dean Ball 也不赞成，但事已至此。

paras.en: A prediction of what the White House will do, or a description of what it is considering doing, is very different from what you think we should do.
paras.zh: 对白宫将要做什麼的预测，或对其正在考虑做什么的描述，与你认为我们应该做什么，是非常不同的。

paras.en: I do think that we should at least consider treating Chinese open models as supply chain risks, and doing things like keeping them out of critical infrastructure, but that is different from what it looks like is being considered.
paras.zh: 我确实认为我们至少应该考虑将中国开放模型视为供应链风险，并采取诸如将其排除在关键基础设施之外的措施，但这与看起来正在被考虑的做法不同。

paras.en: The ones who actually want to ‘ban open models’ are never the ones you think. Remember that all the AI-safety-motivated bills were careful to minimize impact to open models, whereas the White House move will be attempting to maximize impact. Different worlds.
paras.zh: 真正想要‘禁止开放模型’的人从来不是你所想的那样。记住，所有以 AI 安全为动机的法案都小心翼翼地尽量减少对开放模型的影响，而白宫的举动将试图最大化影响。不同的世界。

paras.en: Maria Curi: The Trump administration is showing signs it could ban cutting-edge Chinese AI models — a momentous move that could lock in dominance by OpenAI and Anthropic.
paras.zh: Maria Curi：特朗普政府显示出可能禁止中国尖端 AI 模型的迹象——这是一个重大举措，可能锁定 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的主导地位。

paras.en: Parts of the administration have tried to implement de facto bans on foreign open-source models before, knowledgeable sources tell Axios. Last week's rise of Chinese model Kimi is reigniting those efforts.
paras.zh: 有知情人士向 Axios 透露，政府部分部门此前曾试图对外国开源模型实施事实上的禁令。上周中国模型 Kimi 的崛起正重新点燃这些努力。

paras.en: I was early on the 'Google is no longer in the top tier' train, but there is plenty of healthy competition that is not Chinese. Curi is taking the 'duopoly' and 'lock in' lines directly from David Sacks's disingenuous misreading of Dean Ball's original tweet. OpenAI and Anthropic are not driving this.
paras.zh: 我很早就认为‘谷歌已不在顶级梯队’，但并非只有中国才有大量健康竞争。Curi 直接引用了 David Sacks 对 Dean Ball 原始推文的虚伪误读，来支持‘双头垄断’和‘锁定’的说法。OpenAI 和 Anthropic 并未推动此事。

paras.en: The White House, as per usual, is proposing to do this in a maximally blunt way.
paras.zh: 一如既往，白宫提议以最直截了当的方式来做这件事。

paras.en: The Commerce Department last year considered adding multiple Chinese AI labs to its 'Entity List,' which would effectively cut off U.S. access without a license, a source close to the administration told Axios.
paras.zh: 一位接近政府的消息人士告诉 Axios，商务部去年曾考虑将多家中国 AI 实验室列入其‘实体清单’，这将实际上在没有许可证的情况下切断美国的访问。

paras.en: Dean Ball's prediction, which was also a subtle hint as to how to do it if the White House decided it needed to do it, was simply to create regulatory uncertainty, which would be sufficient to discourage big players from using foreign models in critical places, while letting startups and builders have their fun. A 'supply chain risk' designation would be the next step up from that.
paras.zh: Dean Ball 的预测——这也是一种微妙的暗示，即如果白宫决定需要这样做，该如何做——仅仅是制造监管不确定性，这足以阻止大玩家在关键领域使用外国模型，同时让初创公司和开发者继续玩乐。‘供应链风险’认定将是此基础上的下一步。

paras.en: This proposal is something else. This is a sledgehammer.
paras.zh: 这个提案完全是另一回事。这是一记大锤。

paras.en: The White House considered implementing an executive order stating that U.S. companies could only host Chinese models if they could guarantee security and take on liability if security were breached, the source added.
paras.zh: 消息人士补充说，白宫曾考虑实施一项行政令，规定美国公司只有在能够保证安全、并在安全遭到破坏时承担责任的情况下，才能托管中国模型。

paras.en: … Administration officials keen on keeping regulation from stifling innovation killed all of those efforts.
paras.zh: ……那些希望避免监管扼杀创新的政府官员扼杀了所有这些努力。

paras.en: This is a past proposal I'd heard about privately, and it would be a de facto ban on the cloud providers serving those models. This would also be deeply stupid, driving business to the competition without accomplishing anything.
paras.zh: 这是我私下听说过的一项过往提案，它实际上会构成对那些为这些模型提供服务的云服务商的禁令。这也会极其愚蠢，只会把业务推向竞争对手，却一事无成。

paras.en: I do sympathize with David Sacks that he had to keep pushing back on overreactions like this. That doesn't excuse his actions, but almost everyone in politics has troubles and crazier people of their own to deal with.
paras.zh: 我确实同情 David Sacks，他不得不一再反击这类过度反应。这并不能为他的行为开脱，但政界几乎每个人都有自己的麻烦和更疯狂的人要应付。

paras.en: Instead of a ban, another source familiar with government discussions described a push to highlight potential backdoors and lack of security with Chinese models, and the governance issue that brings.
paras.zh: 另一位熟悉政府讨论的消息人士称，与其说是禁令，不如说是推动强调中国模型可能存在的后门和安全缺失，以及由此带来的治理问题。

paras.en: That's exactly the Dean Ball prediction. That option might be starting to look pretty good right around now, huh?
paras.zh: 这正是 Dean Ball 的预测。现在看来，那个选项可能开始显得相当不错了，是吧？

full.sec: OpenAI Employees Are Relatively Bullish On This One
full.secZh: OpenAI 员工对此相对乐观

paras.en: Okay. Back to Kimi K3's actual capabilities.
paras.zh: 好，回到 Kimi K3 的实际能力上。

paras.en: @viemccoy (OpenAI): Kimi seems to be a true open-weights frontier model. Compared to jailbreaking proprietary models, fine-tuning this to be a malicious coding agent will be trivial since you have the weights.
paras.zh: @viemccoy（OpenAI）：Kimi 似乎是一个真正的开放权重前沿模型。与越狱专有模型相比，由于你拥有权重，将其微调为一个恶意编程智能体将是轻而易举的。

paras.en: We live in a completely different world now.
paras.zh: 我们现在身处一个完全不同的世界。

paras.en: That would be the top end of potential scenarios here.
paras.zh: 那将是这里潜在情景的上限。

paras.en: @viemccoy (OpenAI): I was using Fable as a second eye on frontend, but Kimi K3 has completely blown me away in this regard.
paras.zh: @viemccoy（OpenAI）：我之前用 Fable 作为前端的第二双眼睛，但 Kimi K3 在这方面彻底让我折服。

paras.en: Fable is still the best at philosophy, Sol remains undefeated for any structured task, but k3 ... It has a *je ne sais quoi* that American models don't have.
paras.zh: Fable 在哲学方面仍是最强的，Sol 在任何结构化任务上依然无人能敌，但 k3……它有一种美国模型所不具备的*难以言喻的特质*。

paras.en: roon (OpenAI): the era of the Chinese labs being far behind is over; Kimi is at least on par with the modern public frontier models. People have to think differently now, without any competitive margin built in.
paras.zh: roon（OpenAI）：中国实验室远远落后的时代已经结束，Kimi 至少已与当前公开的前沿模型不相上下。人们现在必须换一种思路，不能再指望任何竞争缓冲空间。

paras.en: Note: in the coming days, I expect that people will find Kimi k3 somewhat less practically useful than today's numbers suggest. However, its reputation will settle as an incredibly powerful model whose open weights are on the web.
paras.zh: 注：在接下来的几天里，我预计人们会发现 Kimi k3 的实际实用性略低于当前这些数字所显示的水平。不过，它的声誉终将稳定为一款极其强大的模型——其开放权重已在网上公开。

paras.en: I agree strongly with Roon's second paragraph. The first one at least toys with jumping the gun; also notice he only is talking about 'public' models.
paras.zh: 我强烈赞同 Roon 的第二段。第一段至少有点操之过急的意味；另外注意，他只谈到了“公开”模型。

full.sec: Kimi K3 Is Relatively Strongest At Typical Agentic Coding, Front End Work and 3D
full.secZh: Kimi K3 在典型智能体式编程、前端工作与 3D 方面相对最强

paras.en: As per Dean Ball above, it is clearly very good for most people's agentic coding, plausibly on par with models from Q1 2026. Most agentic coding is rather close to what benchmarks and training tasks measure, so you can be relatively 'shallow' and still impress in the day to day.
paras.zh: 正如上文 Dean Ball 所言，对于大多数人的智能体式编程来说，它显然非常出色，可能与 2026 年第一季度的模型不相上下。大多数智能体式编程与基准测试和训练任务所衡量的内容相当接近，因此你可以相对“浅薄”却仍在日常工作中令人印象深刻。

paras.en: Jake Halloran: capacity constrained to the point of broad uselessness but when it does work it's near frontier at code stuff, especially design work and much further from the frontier (though still probably the third best lab) on non-code stuff like writing and weird data knowledge.
paras.zh: Jake Halloran：容量受限到广泛无用的程度，但当它确实工作时，在代码方面接近前沿，尤其是设计工作，而在非代码方面（如写作和奇怪的数据知识）则离前沿远得多（尽管可能仍是第三好的实验室）。

paras.en: Tushit runs an internal react/frontend eval, finds Kimi the slowest versus Opus, Sonnet and Grok 4.5 (?) but about half the cost of Opus, and all of them usually succeed, with Grok actually coming out ahead. Sounds like a saturated benchmark, but some people's real world tasks are saturated. Handling the ordinary stuff matters, too.
paras.zh: Tushit 运行了一个内部的 react/前端评估，发现 Kimi 相比 Opus、Sonnet 和 Grok 4.5（？）是最慢的，但成本约为 Opus 的一半，而且它们通常都能成功，Grok 实际上表现更优。听起来像是一个饱和的基准测试，但有些人的现实世界任务已经饱和。处理普通事务也很重要。

paras.en: Thus, some people stick with the saturated benchmarks:
paras.zh: 因此，有些人坚持使用饱和的基准测试：

paras.en: Medo42: 100% on my usual (non-agentic) coding task, but not the first open model to achieve that. Good presentation of the result and approach along with the code. Good vision, but not beating Gemini. Smells big. Runs slow.
paras.zh: Medo42：在我通常的（非智能体式）编程任务上达到 100%，但不是第一个实现这一点的开源模型。结果和方法的展示以及代码都很好。视觉能力不错，但没超过 Gemini。感觉规模很大。运行缓慢。

paras.en: Also we've seen a bunch of 3D stuff that looks cool.
paras.zh: 此外，我们还看到了一些看起来很酷的 3D 相关内容。

paras.en: Theo - t3.gg: Kimi K3 is so good at 3D stuff, holy shit.
paras.zh: Theo - t3.gg：Kimi K3 在 3D 方面太强了，天哪。

paras.en: So far I just have it doing stupid three.js stuff in the browser. Will have it try Blender later when I have time; currently late to a ton of shit.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，我只是让它在浏览器里做一些简单的 three.js 东西。等我有时间再让它试试 Blender；现在手头一堆事都来不及做。

paras.en: FWIW, Fable and 5.6 both sucked hard at three.js modeling, and weren't meaningfully better in Blender. Kimi is way ahead from my limited testing.
paras.zh: 顺便说一句，Fable 和 5.6 在 three.js 建模方面都很差劲，在 Blender 里也没有明显更好。就我有限的测试来看，Kimi 要领先得多。

paras.en: Here is the opposite opinion, though; reactions always vary:
paras.zh: 不过，这里也有相反的意见；大家的反应总是各不相同：

paras.en: paperclippriors: Found little reason to use it over Fable or 5.6 for coding. It is, however, an absolute *delight* to talk to. Big model smell, very Claude-like but somewhat more enthusiastic and less constrained. Feels like they have a strong base
paras.zh: paperclippriors：在编程方面，相比 Fable 或 5.6，找不到太多使用它的理由。不过，和它对话绝对是一种*愉悦*。很有“大模型味”，非常像 Claude，但更热情一些、约束更少。感觉他们有一个很强的基础。

paras.en: **AllTime:** You can feel it's a big model. It's smart and quite good at deduction, has impressive knowledge though the breadth might not quite be on the level of the American frontier models. Thinks too much on many problems unless instructed otherwise, and even then sometimes. Impressive!
paras.zh: **AllTime：** 你能感觉到这是一个大模型。它很聪明，推理能力相当不错，知识储备令人印象深刻，尽管知识广度可能还达不到美国前沿模型的水平。在许多问题上思考过度，除非另有指示，而且即便有指示有时也仍会如此。令人印象深刻！

paras.en: **Aivo:** Pleasant to talk to. Pretty okay writer. I haven't done any coding with it so far.
paras.zh: **Aivo：** 交流起来很愉快。写作水平还算可以。到目前为止我还没用它做过任何编程。

paras.en: **Echo Nolan:** On a tough ML design problem it gave a result that is complicated and unworkable where gpt-5.6-pro gave a result that is complicated and workable and fable gave a result that is pleasantly simpler and workable.
paras.zh: **Echo Nolan：** 在一个困难的机器学习设计问题上，它给出的结果复杂且不可行；而 gpt-5.6-pro 给出的结果复杂但可行，fable 给出的结果则令人愉快地更简单且可行。

paras.en: The biggest claim would be that it lives up to its benchmarks. Elanor is explicitly claiming this, although almost everyone else disagrees.
paras.zh: 最大的主张莫过于它名副其实地达到了其基准测试成绩。Elanor 明确这样主张，尽管几乎其他所有人都不同意。

paras.en: **Eleanor Berger:** Very good and complete and balanced model. Impressive that they got this level of intelligence and finesse without it resorting to an endless internal monologue — it's not as efficient as Sol or even Fable, but it's also not a GLM. Great for all tasks, from coding to writing, to agentic workflows. Actually has good taste.
paras.zh: **Eleanor Berger：** 非常好、完整且均衡的模型。令人印象深刻的是，他们达到了这种水平的智能与精细度，却没有诉诸无休止的内部独白——它不如 Sol 甚至 Fable 高效，但它也不是 GLM。适用于所有任务，从编程到写作，再到智能体式工作流。实际上很有品味。

paras.en: This is the first Chinese/open model that feels like it belongs where the benchmarks place it. It rightly occupies the top 3 with Sol and Fable. The service quality is terrible, but hopefully once they release the weights there will be many more options, including ones that are hosted in the free world. The world has changed meaningfully with the release of this model. I will be using it a lot once it's available from more reliable servers.
paras.zh: 这是第一个让人感觉其表现与基准测试排名相符的中国/开源模型。它与 Sol 和 Fable 一同位居前三，实至名归。服务质量很糟糕，但希望一旦他们发布权重，就会有更多选择，包括托管在自由世界的选项。随着这个模型的发布，世界已经发生了实质性的变化。一旦它能在更可靠的服务器上使用，我会大量使用它。

paras.en: Petr Baudis: Finally got my first two Kimi K3 reps in! Same tasks I had Fable do in another worktree (patching @MuaddibLLM a pi-based harness).
paras.zh: Petr Baudis：终于完成了我的前两次 Kimi K3 测试！任务与我在另一个工作树中让 Fable 做的相同（修补 @MuaddibLLM 一个基于 pi 的测试框架）。

paras.en: It did an ok-ish job, but with serious deficiencies compared to Fable. A review by Sol would equalize, though.
paras.zh: 它完成得还算可以，但与 Fable 相比存在严重缺陷。不过，由 Sol 进行评审将会使二者持平。

paras.en: On a break, it then drew a dickpic (inadvertently), which was certainly a first. (When I pointed it out, it eventually "saw" it but I think it actually didn't, based on its own... description.)
paras.zh: 在休息时，它随后（无意中）画了一幅不雅图，这绝对是头一遭。（当我指出这一点时，它最终“看到”了，但根据它自己的……描述，我认为它实际上并没有看到。）

paras.en: Daniel Mulec: It's really no Fable competitor but it's worlds apart from the garbage that 2.6 used to be. Enjoying it but it's in a weird spot. It's neither good enough to replace Fable or GPT-5.6 for me nor good enough to just be an executor model for implementation plans created by GPT-5.6 either.
paras.zh: Daniel Mulec：它确实不是 Fable 的竞争对手，但与 2.6 曾经的垃圾表现相比已是天壤之别。我很喜欢它，但它处于一个尴尬的位置。对我来说，它既不足以取代 Fable 或 GPT-5.6，也不足以仅仅作为执行 GPT-5.6 所创建实现计划的执行模型。

paras.en: Seems like with everything I do with K3, K3 always only gets there 70-90% of what I actually want and need (79-90% of each and every prompt).
paras.zh: 似乎我用 K3 做的每件事，K3 总是只达到我实际想要和需要的 70-90%（每个提示词的 79-90%）。

paras.en: Inadvertent. Right. Let's see the J-space.
paras.zh: 无意为之。对。让我们看看 J-space。

paras.en: Matt Bruenig: OpenCode with Kimi K3 can execute my NLRB Research skill very well. It is quite a bit slower than Anthropic/Claude but you can just set it off and do something else while it churns, I suppose.
paras.zh: Matt Bruenig：用 Kimi K3 运行 OpenCode 能很好地执行我的 NLRB Research 技能。它比 Anthropic/Claude 慢不少，但我想你可以直接把它启动起来，在它慢慢跑的时候去做别的事。
